14D.4 You shall eat no manner of fat from any animal.
14D.6 You shall not eat any manner of blood from fowl or beast either by itself or with its flesh.

precepts.text: The flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten the same day that it is offered. You had to eat these offerings; touch, taste, and handle belong to that service.
precepts.point: Touch not; taste not; handle not; which all are to perish with the using; after the commandments and doctrines of men. Stop following man. Christ has come; he taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary and his sacrifice is supreme.
precepts.why:
Paul asks, “why, as though living in the world, are ye subject to ordinances, (Touch not; taste not; handle not”. Why are you going back to those ordinances? He has not changed the subject since verse 14, “Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us”, and those ordinances are the “carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation” of Hebrews 9:10: until the time of Christ.

Leviticus shows what touch, taste and handle belong to: “the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten the same day that it is offered; he shall not leave any of it until the morning. But if the sacrifice of his offering be a vow, or a voluntary offering, it shall be eaten the same day that he offereth his sacrifice: and on the morrow also the remainder of it shall be eaten”. You had to eat these offerings. Eating, eating: that is the touching, tasting and handling of the sacrifice.

So when Colossians 2:21 says “Touch not; taste not; handle not”, it is saying leave it alone. The men beguiling the believers were rejecting Christ, saying the animal is above Christ: you need that goat, you need that lamb, that ram, that ox, that bull. Paul was saying no, Christ is above all. He taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary, and his sacrifice is supreme.

precepts.text: The fat forbidden is the fat of the beast of which men offer an offering made by fire; it belongs to the laws of sacrifice.
precepts.point: Leviticus 7 answers it in context: whosoever eateth the fat of the beast of which men offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord shall be cut off. This is the law of sacrifice, which we are no longer under; Christ is the end of the law for righteousness. The sacrifices stopped after 70 AD at the fall of Jerusalem, when there was no longer a temple. And there is no way to take off all the fat of the meat you eat; we are not koshering our meat.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
Brothers and sisters ask whether we are cut off for eating fat. Having that question is a good thing; it means you are reading to understand, not reading just to say you read four chapters. Leviticus 7 answers it in context.

“Ye shall eat no manner of fat, of ox, or of sheep, or of goat. And the fat of the beast that dieth of itself, and the fat of that which is torn with beasts, may be used in any other use: but ye shall in no wise eat of it. For whosoever eateth the fat of the beast, of which men offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord, even the soul that eateth it shall be cut off from his people.”

The fat forbidden is the fat of the beast of which men offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord. This belongs to the law of sacrifice, which we are no longer under. And there is no way to take off all the fat of the meat you eat; we are not koshering our meat.

precepts.text: Ye shall eat no manner of blood; whatsoever soul eateth any manner of blood shall be cut off from his people.
precepts.point: The Lord put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel and sanctified his people with these laws; these laws make us special, going back to Deuteronomy 7 and 6, how he separated us. Do not follow the customs and fashions of the heathen.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
The blood is the other half of the perpetual statute, and it reads wider than the fat: “ye shall eat no manner of blood, whether it be of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings. Whatsoever soul it be that eateth any manner of blood, even that soul shall be cut off from his people.”

The blood was also for the altar of the Lord, but it is no manner of blood, of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings, and there is more to why the Lord had to say it: what Israel had learned in Egypt.

precepts.text: You hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; God, who is rich in mercy, even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ; by grace ye are saved.
precepts.point: By grace ye are saved means all of us deserve death for our sins, but through Christ we have grace and are saved from the destruction to come, if we endure to the end keeping the commandments.
precepts.why:
Paul was a master of the law, and trespass in his letters goes back to this law of the trespass offering: “you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”. The prince of the power of the air is Satan.

“Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others. But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;)”

By grace ye are saved means all of us deserve death for our sins, but through Christ we have grace and are saved from the destruction to come, if we endure to the end keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ; that is the grace, that we are not killed for our sins.
precepts.point: By grace ye are saved means all of us deserve death for our sins, but through Christ we have grace and are saved from the destruction to come, if we endure to the end keeping the commandments.
precepts.why:
Paul says “the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

That is the grace: we are not killed for our sins. The trespass offering, one law with the sin offering, most holy, is what stood between the trespasser and death; now the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ, if we endure to the end keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not, when they defile my tabernacle; the uncleanness laws guarded the sacrifice.
precepts.point: All the touching of unclean and defiled things pertains to sacrifice: the point of the uncleanness laws was to separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not when they defile the tabernacle. There is no more sacrifice, so those defilement laws do not apply today; a brother can brush his hair with a brush of boar bristles, because that law was about coming in to sacrifice.
precepts.why:
All the touching of unclean and defiled things pertains to sacrifice. “Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness; that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is among them.”

An unclean man coming into the tabernacle to sacrifice or a priest eating unclean was facing death before the Lord; that is why the flesh that touched any unclean thing was burnt with fire and the soul that ate of the peace offerings with his uncleanness upon him was cut off. The uncleanness laws guarded the sacrifice.

There is no more sacrifice, so those defilement laws do not apply today. A brother can brush his hair with a brush of boar bristles, because that law was about coming in to sacrifice.

precepts.text: Though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me; soap was known in Israel of old, made from the fat.
precepts.point: But blood was different: no manner of blood, of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings, whether sacrificing or not. The soul that eats any manner of blood shall be cut off; cook the food well done, not rare, and that stands to this day.
precepts.why:
The fat of the beast that dieth of itself and of that which is torn with beasts may be used in any other use, and one of those other uses was soap: Israel took the fat and made soap with it. Jeremiah shows it: “though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God.”

Israel had soap way back then and did not live filthy, and when the Moors ruled in Europe they introduced soap to Esau again.

The fat pertained to the sacrifices, burnt completely or put to other uses like this, so there is no sin in eating fat off an animal now. Blood is different: no manner of blood, of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings, whether sacrificing or not, and that stands to this day.

precepts.text: Sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up; the offering was lifted and waved before the Lord.
precepts.point: The wave breast and the heave shoulder were given to Aaron the priest and his sons by a statute for ever; this is how the priests ate from the peace offerings. Leviticus 10 returns to these portions, the wave breast and heave shoulder given to Aaron and his sons and daughters; chapters 6 through 10 explain the offerings.
precepts.why:
Moses was told, “thou shalt sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up, of the ram of the consecration, even of that which is for Aaron, and of that which is for his sons”.

Which is waved, and which is heaved up: the offering was lifted and waved before the Lord as a sign, proof of what the man had brought with his own hands. The wave breast and the heave shoulder then belonged to Aaron and his sons by a statute for ever; this is how the priests ate from the peace offerings, and Leviticus 10 returns to these same portions.

precepts.text: Ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ: for he is our peace, who hath abolished in his flesh the law of commandments contained in ordinances, and reconciled both unto God in one body.
precepts.point: The law of sacrifice was contrary to us because those sacrifices offered year by year continually could never make the comers thereunto perfect. It was a scapegoat so the law would not have to kill us; the Most High has been extending grace since Adam, for he had every right to kill Adam and Eve, and instead extended grace through the animal sacrifice. If the law of sacrifice still stood, there would be no sacrifice for worshipping other gods, and we would be done as a people; it was taken out of the way so Israel could come back to God.
precepts.why:
Verse 37 lists all the offerings in one place, and Christ is our peace offering between us and the Most High: “now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us”.

“Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances”. The ordinances are the law of sacrifice: sprinkle the blood seven times, a lamb without blemish, eaten before the third day, carried without the camp, burnt to ashes with the garments changed. He abolished that in his flesh, “that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby”.

precepts.text: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, nailing it to his cross; let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.
precepts.point: The law of sacrifice was contrary to us because those sacrifices offered year by year continually could never make the comers thereunto perfect. It was a scapegoat so the law would not have to kill us; the Most High has been extending grace since Adam, for he had every right to kill Adam and Eve, and instead extended grace through the animal sacrifice. If the law of sacrifice still stood, there would be no sacrifice for worshipping other gods, and we would be done as a people; it was taken out of the way so Israel could come back to God.
precepts.why:
“Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross”. The handwriting of ordinances is the law of sacrifice listed in Leviticus 7:37.

“Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” Add the word offering: the meat offering and drink offering we just read in Leviticus. No man can condemn you because you are not sacrificing animals any more, or for how you observe a holyday, new moon, or sabbath pertaining to sacrifice, for those are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ.

precepts.text: The law having a shadow of good things to come can never with those sacrifices year by year make the comers thereunto perfect; that is how it was contrary to us.
precepts.point: The law of sacrifice was contrary to us because those sacrifices offered year by year continually could never make the comers thereunto perfect. It was a scapegoat so the law would not have to kill us; the Most High has been extending grace since Adam, for he had every right to kill Adam and Eve, and instead extended grace through the animal sacrifice. If the law of sacrifice still stood, there would be no sacrifice for worshipping other gods, and we would be done as a people; it was taken out of the way so Israel could come back to God.
precepts.why:
This is how the law of sacrifice was contrary to us: “the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.”

It was a scapegoat so the law would not have to kill us. The Most High has been extending grace since Adam, for He had every right to kill Adam and Eve, and instead extended grace through the animal sacrifice.

If the law of sacrifice still stood, there would be no sacrifice for worshipping other gods, and we would be done as a people; it was taken out of the way so Israel could come back to God.

precepts.text: The fat with the breast is brought and the breast waved for a wave offering before the Lord; that is the wave offering of this passage.
precepts.point: The wave offering is explained in chapter 7: his own hands shall bring the offerings of the Lord made by fire, the fat with the breast, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the Lord.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

precepts.why:
Moses told Aaron, Eleazar and Ithamar that the wave breast and heave shoulder were theirs to eat in a clean place, “thou, and thy sons, and thy daughters with thee”, their due by a statute for ever. Chapter 7 explains what the wave offering is.

“His own hands shall bring the offerings of the Lord made by fire, the fat with the breast, it shall he bring, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the Lord.” The man bringing his peace offering carries the fat with the breast, and the breast is waved before the Lord.

That is the wave breast of Leviticus 10:14-15, brought “with the offerings made by fire of the fat, to wave it for a wave offering before the Lord”, and given to Aaron and his sons as their portion.

points: Likewise this is the law of the trespass offering: it is most holy. The fat, the rump, the fat that covers the inwards, the kidneys, and the caul above the liver, basically the guts, were burnt upon the altar, and as the sin offering is, so is the trespass offering; there is one law for them.

Paul was a master of the law, and trespass in his letters goes back to this law: you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins, when in time past we walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, which is Satan.
This is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings. If it was offered for a thanksgiving, the flesh was eaten the same day it was offered; none was left until the morning.

If the sacrifice was a vow or a voluntary offering, it was eaten the same day and the remainder on the morrow also; that is the difference between the two. But flesh remaining on the third day was burnt with fire, and if any was eaten on the third day it was an abomination, and the offering was not accepted.

The flesh that touched any unclean thing was not eaten but burnt with fire, and the soul that ate of the peace offerings having his uncleanness upon him was cut off from his people. An unclean man coming into the tabernacle to sacrifice or a priest eating unclean was facing death before the Lord.

All the touching of unclean and defiled things pertains to sacrifice: the point of the uncleanness laws was to separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not when they defile the tabernacle. There is no more sacrifice, so those defilement laws do not apply today; a brother can brush his hair with a brush of boar bristles, because that law was about coming in to sacrifice.

Ye shall eat no manner of fat, of ox, or of sheep, or of goat: this pertained to the sacrifices. The fat upon the sacrifices was either burnt completely or put to other uses; there is no sin in eating fat off an animal now, because what it pertained to was the sacrifice.

One of those other uses was soap: Israel took the fat and made soap with it. Jeremiah shows it, though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap; Israel had soap way back then and did not live filthy, and when the Moors ruled in Europe they introduced soap to Esau again.

But blood was different: no manner of blood, of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings, whether sacrificing or not. The soul that eats any manner of blood shall be cut off; cook the food well done, not rare, and that stands to this day.

He that offered his peace offerings brought the oblation with his own hands: the fat with the breast, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the LORD. The wave offering was heaved up and waved before the Lord as a sign, proof of what he had brought.

The wave breast and the heave shoulder were given to Aaron the priest and his sons by a statute for ever; this is how the priests ate from the peace offerings. Leviticus 10 returns to these portions, the wave breast and heave shoulder given to Aaron and his sons and daughters; chapters 6 through 10 explain the offerings.

Verse 37 lists all the different offerings in one place: the burnt offering, the meat offering, the sin offering, the trespass offering, the consecrations, and the sacrifice of the peace offerings, which the LORD commanded Moses in mount Sinai.

Christ is our peace, our peace offering between us and the Most High. He abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; the ordinances are the law of sacrifice, sprinkle the blood seven times, a lamb without blemish, eaten before the third day, carried without the camp, burnt to ashes with the garments changed.

Let no man therefore judge you in meat or in drink: add the word offering, the meat offering and drink offering we just read in Leviticus. No man can condemn you because you are not sacrificing animals any more, or for how you observe a holyday, new moon, or sabbath pertaining to sacrifice, for those are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ.

The law of sacrifice was contrary to us because those sacrifices offered year by year continually could never make the comers thereunto perfect. It was a scapegoat so the law would not have to kill us; the Most High has been extending grace since Adam, for he had every right to kill Adam and Eve, and instead extended grace through the animal sacrifice. If the law of sacrifice still stood, there would be no sacrifice for worshipping other gods, and we would be done as a people; it was taken out of the way so Israel could come back to God.
